To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) chronic stress induces a decrease in dopamine (DA) levels in the nucleus accumbens, an effect that is mediated by glucocorticoids (GCs) and is accompanied by a decrease in DA turnover; 2) chronic stress increases the vulnerability of DA neurons to psychostimulants, and that this increased vulnerability is also mediated by GCs; and 3) chronic stress decreases the number of DA neurons in the substantia nigra and ventral tegmental area

the vulnerability to develop drug addiction is related to the ability to regulate the activity of mesencephalic DA neurons, an ability which is in turn determined by the level of glucocorticoids and the degree of environmental stress.
stress and glucocorticoids are important factors determining vulnerability to psychotomimetic drugs.
